newsitem.title: JAPAN: Seiko sees higher 1997/98 parent profit.
newsitem.headline: Seiko sees higher 1997/98 parent profit.

text.p: Seiko Corp on Thursday forecast a parent current profit of 6.50 billion yen in the year to March 31, 1998, up from an estimated 2.50 billion yen in 1996/97.
The increase reflects expectations of higher sales and exports of wrist watches, a Seiko spokesman said. The final figure for 1996/97 is expected to be announced in May.

Despite the rise in profits, parent sales in 1997/98 are forecast to fall to 170 billion yen from an estimated 192 billion in 1996/97, because the company plans to sell its jewellery division to a new subsidiary on July 1 this year, the spokesman said.
Seiko will shift its jewellery division to a new subsidiary, Seiko Jewellery Co, that will be set up on May 1. Seiko hopes the move will improve management and sales of its jewellery business.
Seiko said its jewellery division is expected to post a current loss of 600 million yen in 1996/97 on sales of 14.7 billion.
Seiko also forecast a parent current profit for 1998/99 of 7.50 billion yen on sales of 165 billion yen.
Parent current profit totalled 1.10 billion yen in 1995/96 on sales of 215.82 billion yen.
